Potent

POH-tnt · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Potent is powerful in effect or strength.

The new antibiotic proved potent against infections that older drugs couldn't touch.

Worked Example

Chili oil is so potent that a single drop can transform an entire pot of soup.

A tiny amount produces a huge result -- that concentrated strength is exactly what potent describes.

How Strong Is It? — strong → potent → overpowering

strong vs. potent

strong vs. potent: Strong is the everyday word -- potent emphasizes concentrated power: medicine, arguments, smells.

overpowering vs. potent

overpowering vs. potent: Overpowering goes past potent -- so strong it overwhelms everything else around it.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — pot-

root — pot-: able; having power (from potens, posse) (Latin)

suffix — -ent

suffix — -ent: adjective-forming: in a state of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Pot- ('able, power') + -ent: potent literally means 'having power' -- the same root gives us potential (power not yet used) and omnipotent (all-powerful).

Use the root in a new word: potential

Use the root in a new word: potential: The scout insisted the young pitcher had the potential to reach the major leagues.

Root Check

Word Choice

Potent works for anything whose power is strongly felt -- medicine, poison, arguments, symbols, smells. It's a notch more formal than 'strong,' and it hints that the power is concentrated.
